rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies the seven heavens as seven corresponding layers of the corporeal cosmos, with the star-and-planet realm nearest Earth.
rows.anchor: أن هذه السماوات السبع المذكورة جميعا من الخلق الجسماني فكأنها طبقات سبع متطابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearest heaven is the realm of stars and planets; the Quran describes the other six only as layered.
rows.anchor: أقربها منا عالم النجوم والكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven heavens do not mean the celestial bodies generally or particular bodies such as the sun and moon.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد بالسماوات السبع الأجرام العلوية أو خصوص بعضها كالشمس والقمر أو غيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports about angels dwelling in heaven, descending with commands, ascending with records, barred gates, and descending provisions imply a distinct relation to these heavens.
rows.anchor: وأن للسماء أبوابا لا تفتح للكفار وأن الأشياء والأرزاق تنزل منها وغير ذلك مما تشير إليه متفرقات الآيات والروايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ heavenly order is unlike the material placement and changing physical order that governs bodies in the visible cosmos.
rows.anchor: يكشف عن أن لهذه الأمور نوع تعلق بهذه السماوات لا كتعلق ما نراه من الأجسام بمحالها وأماكنها الجسمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible celestial bodies have elemental, bodily existence and physical laws like those of the earthly world, unlike the heavenly order described for angels.
rows.anchor: أن لهذه الأجرام العلوية كائنة ما كانت كينونة عنصرية جسمانية تجري فيها نظائر الأحكام والآثار الجارية في عالمنا الأرضي العنصري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that angels are created from light, subsist on glorification, and have described forms support the distinction between their world and the physical cosmos.
rows.anchor: ما ورد أن الملائكة خلقوا من نور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He understands the seven heavens as seven ordered malakūt worlds of angels; their attributes are ascribed to visible heavens because of their height and encompassing relation to Earth, to aid simple understanding.
rows.anchor: فللملائكة عوالم ملكوتية سبعة مترتبة سميت سماوات سبعا ونسبت ما لها من الخواص والآثار إلى ظاهر هذه السماوات

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports that Quraysh chose ʿUtba b. Rabiʿa, their expert in magic, soothsaying, and poetry, to confront Muhammad; ʿUtba offered wealth or marriage if those were his motives.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال اجتمع قريش يوما فقالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuing Jabir’s account, the Prophet asks ʿUtba if he is finished, recites Fussilat through the warning of a thunderbolt, and is stopped; ʿUtba says he understood only the warning.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فرغت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other routes give variant wording; one has ʿUtba say he had never heard such speech and that it was neither poetry, magic, nor soothsaying, and that it would have news.
rows.anchor: قال والله إني قد سمعت قولا ما سمعت بمثله قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes a separate report that the Prophet recited the sūra’s opening to al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra, deferring its account to the commentary on 74:11.
rows.anchor: وفي تلاوته صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم آيات أول السورة على وليد بن المغيرة رواية أخرى

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reports that Jews asked what God created during six days; the Prophet described the creation of Earth, mountains, settlements and provisions, heavens and angels, then the appointed times, calamity, and Adam on Friday.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن أبي بكر قال جاء اليهود إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقالوا يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Similar versions are also attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām, ʿIkrima, and others, as well as appearing in some Shiʿi reports.
rows.anchor: وروى ما يقرب منه عن ابن عباس وعبد الله بن سلام وعن عكرمة وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews’ claim that the Prophet had spoken truth if he completed the account meant they expected him to say God finished creation and rested on Saturday.
rows.anchor: قالوا صدقت إن تممت أي تممت كلامك في الخلق بأن تقول إنه تعالى فرغ من الخلق يوم السبت واستراح فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He objects that the report’s creation order plainly contradicts Genesis: its sequence places light, heavens, Earth, luminaries, animals, and humanity on different days, with rest on Saturday.
rows.anchor: وهو مخالف لما ورد في أول سفر التكوين من التوراة مخالفة صريحة ففيها أنه خلق النور والظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He dismisses the proposed defense that the Torah now differs from the Torah in the Prophet’s time as untenable.
rows.anchor: والقول بأن التوراة الحاضرة غير ما كان في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A weekday depends on one rotation of Earth relative to the sun, so the report’s account of creating Earth before the heavens and sun makes its first days incoherent.
rows.anchor: اليوم من الأسبوع وهو نهار مع ليلته يتوقف في كينونته على حركة الأرض الوضعية دورة واحدة قبال الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same problem applies to creating the heavens and sun when there is no sun by which to define a day.
rows.anchor: ونظير الإشكال جار في خلق السماء والسماويات ومنها الشمس ولا يوم حيث لا شمس بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report assigns a day to mountains, settlements, rivers, and provisions, although scientific investigation establishes that mountains form gradually and the same issue applies to the other items.
rows.anchor: وقد جزم الفحص العلمي بأنها تخلق تدريجا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir reports that water was the source of all things, wind arose from water and produced Earth’s foam, and fire then produced smoke from which a clear heaven was made.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام أنه قال وخلق الشيء الذي جميع الأشياء منه وهو الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says other reports convey a similar account of creation.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه المعنى بعض روايات أخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report and Quranic descriptions might be fitted to current scientific accounts of the world, but he avoids defining Quranic truths through scientific hypotheses until proof makes them certain.
rows.anchor: تركنا ذلك احترازا من تحديد الحقائق القرآنية بالأحداس والفرضيات العلمية ما دامت فرضية غير مقطوع بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passage in Nahj al-Balāgha describes the heavens as firmly established without supports, answering God obediently, and serving as the Throne’s place, angels’ abode, and ascent for good words and deeds.
rows.anchor: وفي نهج البلاغة فمن شواهد خلقه خلق السماوات موطدات بلا عمد قائمات بلا سند

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a letter answering al-Fuḍayl al-Rassān, al-Ṣādiq says the stars secure heaven’s inhabitants; when the stars disappear, what they were promised will come.
rows.anchor: فكتب إليه أبو عبد الله عليه السلام إن الكواكب جعلت أمانا لأهل السماء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet compares the People of his Household to the stars: they secure his community, and when they are gone what the community was promised will come.
rows.anchor: جعل أهل بيتي أمانا لأمتي فإذا ذهب أهل بيتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes that this comparison of the Household’s security to the stars is found in more than one report.
rows.anchor: وورد هذا المعنى في غير واحد من الروايات

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ibn Nubāta reports that ʿAlī answered a question about the distance between heaven and Earth: it is the reach of sight and the supplication of the wronged.
rows.anchor: كم بين السماء والأرض؟ قال مد البصر ودعوة المظلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls ʿAlī’s answer an elegant allusion to heaven’s outward and inward dimensions.
rows.anchor: وهو من لطائف كلامه عليه السلام يشير به إلى ظاهر السماء وباطنها كما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nazgh means pricking an animal’s side or hindquarters with a stick to incite it.
rows.anchor: النزغ النخس وهو غرز جنب الدابة أو مؤخرها بقضيب ونحوه ليهيج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mā in immā is extra; the underlying construction is wa-in yanzaghannaka fastʿidh.
rows.anchor: زائدة والأصل وإن ينزغنك فاستعذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The agent of the provocation may be Satan himself or his prompting and whispering.
rows.anchor: والنازغ هو الشيطان أو تسويله ووسوسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers Satan himself as the agent, since Satan cannot whisper to the Prophet directly but can stir the unbelieving addressees into greater rejection, hostility, and harm.
rows.anchor: والأول هو الأنسب لمقام النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فإنه لا سبيل للشيطان إليه بالوسوسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the escalation of hostility to Jacob’s description of Satan stirring between him and his brothers.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله من بعد أن نزغ الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites the verse about Satan casting into a messenger’s aspiration as a possible link if nazgh is taken as Satanic whispering.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول ولا نبي إلا إذا تمنى ألقى الشيطان في أمنيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the second interpretation is adopted, the command must be a general directive completing the instruction, in the rhetorical form “I address you but mean your neighbor.”
rows.anchor: ولو حمل على الوجه الثاني فالمتعين حمله على مطلق الدستور تتميما للأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAwth, ʿiyādh, maʿādh, and istiʿādha all mean seeking refuge or resort.
rows.anchor: والاستعاذة بمعنى وهو الالتجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may be described as hearing the Prophet’s plea and knowing his condition, or hearing people’s words and knowing their deeds.
rows.anchor: السميع لمسألتك العليم بحالك أو السميع لأقوالكم العليم بأفعالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After affirming the call’s goodness and directing the Prophet to answer well, the passage returns to the original invitation and argues for divine unity and resurrection through three signs.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر سبحانه كون دعوته صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أحسن القول ووصاه أن يدفع بأحسن الخصال عاد إلى أصل الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night, day, sun, and moon show one governing order, hence one Lord; that unity entails worshipping Him alone.
rows.anchor: وحدة التدبير واتصاله على وحدة الرب المدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition answers the implied question of what to do: the sun and moon are created and governed, so worship and prostrate only to their Creator.
rows.anchor: فقيل لا تسجدوا للشمس ولا للقمر هما مخلوقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists generally venerated the sun and moon, though it is said that only the Sabeans worshipped them.
rows.anchor: وعامة الوثنيين كانوا يعظمون الشمس والقمر وإن لم يعبدهما غير الصابئين على ما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine plural pronoun refers to the night, day, sun, and moon.
rows.anchor: لليل والنهار والشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship of God is incompatible with worship of anyone else.
rows.anchor: أي إن عبادته لا تجامع عبادة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those near their Lord who glorify Him without weariness are angels and God’s sincere servants; saʾama means boredom.
rows.anchor: الملائكة والمخلصون من عباد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage continues the discussion of provision in 42:19 and follows the statement in 42:12 that God expands and restricts provision.
rows.anchor: متصل بحديث الرزق المذكور في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious guidance is also a provision God gives believers, so discussion of provision folds back into the sūra’s subject of revelation.
rows.anchor: من الرزق نعمة الدين التي آتاها الله سبحانه عباده المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ensuing signs of unity tied to provision include creating the heavens and Earth, spreading creatures, ships at sea, and granting children or barrenness as He wills.
rows.anchor: ثم يذكر بعض آيات التوحيد المتعلقة بالرزق كخلق السماوات والأرض وبث الدواب فيهما والسفائن الجواري في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse contrasts fleeting worldly provision with the better, lasting provision of the afterlife, then turns to believers’ qualities and the fate of wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: من الرزق ما آتاهموه في الدنيا وهو متاعها الفاني بفنائها ومنه ما يخص المؤمنين في الآخرة وهو خير وأبقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verses also contain summaries of rulings, warnings, admonition, calls to truth, and many points of doctrine.
rows.anchor: من إجمال بعض الأحكام والإنذار والتخويف والدعوة إلى الحق وحقائق المعارف شيء كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qadr here is the opposite of expansion: restriction, as in the earlier statement that God expands and restricts provision.
rows.anchor: القدر مقابل البسط معناه التضييق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadr, with either vowel on the dāl, means an amount or measure, or setting something to a determined measure; he cites 77:23 for the latter usage.
rows.anchor: والقدر بفتح الدال وسكونها كمية الشيء وهندسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-baghy means injustice or wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: والبغي الظلم، وقوله { بعباده }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit phrase “His servants” in place of a pronoun points to why God knows them: they are His created servants, sustained by Him and not hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير، والنكتة فيه الإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier wording “for His servants” likewise hints at the grant of provision: a servant’s provision comes from his master.
rows.anchor: لا يخلو من إشارة إلى بيان إيتاء الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God made everyone’s provision abundant enough to satisfy them, they would tyrannize because wealth tends to produce pride, ingratitude, arrogance, and transgression; he links this to 96:6–7.
rows.anchor: من طبع سعة المال الأشر والبطر والاستكبار والطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God apportions what each servant deserves and what will improve that servant’s condition, whether wealth or poverty, because He knows them fully.
rows.anchor: فيعلم ما يستحقه كل عبد وما يصلحه من غنى أو فقر فيؤتيه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The baseline divine practice is to measure provision with regard to what will set people’s condition right; their welfare affects the amount allotted.
rows.anchor: بيان للسنة الإلهية في إيتاء الرزق بالنظر إلى صلاح حال الناس أي إن لصلاح حالهم أثرا في تقدير أرزاقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prosperity of some wealthy wrongdoers does not refute this rule, since a separate rule makes wealth and children a trial.
rows.anchor: وهي سنة الابتلاء والامتحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another rule is entrapment and gradual reprieve, by which God increases the resources of some wrongdoers without their awareness.
rows.anchor: وسنة أخرى هي سنة المكر والاستدراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reforming measure is the initial rule; God may test people, or change His treatment after they change themselves and turn blessing into ingratitude.
rows.anchor: فسنة الإصلاح بتقدير الرزق سنة ابتدائيه يصلح بها حال الإنسان إلا أن يمتحنه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Material blessings, children, true knowledge, and revealed laws are all apportioned forms of provision, including the process of receiving and practicing revelation.
rows.anchor: كذلك المعارف الحقة والشرائع السماوية المنتهية إلى الوحي من حيث إنزالها ومن حيث الابتلاء بها والتلبس بالعمل بها من الرزق المقسوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revealing all comprehensive religious knowledge and law at once would overwhelm people; God instead sent it gradually, preparing acceptance step by step.
rows.anchor: لكن الله سبحانه أنزلها على رسوله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم تدريجا وعلى مكث وهيأ بذلك الناس بقبول بعضها لقبول بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If higher meanings hidden within plain religious teaching were exposed to everyone, all but a rare few would fail to bear them; God communicates according to each person’s understanding and capacity.
rows.anchor: كلمهم في ذلك نوع تكليم يستفيد منه كل على قدر فهمه وسعة صدره كما قال في مثل ضربه في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain-and-valleys parable in 13:17 illustrates how people receive higher meanings according to their capacities.
rows.anchor: أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أوديه بقدرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious duties are distributed according to people’s different trials; assigning every duty to everyone would burden them beyond what they could bear.
rows.anchor: لو كلف بجميعها جميع الناس لتحرجوا منها ولم يتحملوها لكنه سبحانه قسمها بينهم حسب تقسيم الابتلاءات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious knowledge and laws, like material provision, are allotted to people according to what will improve their condition.
rows.anchor: فالرزق بالمعارف والشرائع من أي جهة فرض كالرزق الصوري مفروز بين الناس مقدر على حسب صلاح حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qanūṭ means despair, and ghayth means rain.
rows.anchor: القنوط اليأس، والغيث المطر، قال

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān distinguishes ghayth as rain beneficial in its season, while maṭar can be beneficial or harmful, in or out of season.
rows.anchor: قال في مجمع البيان الغيث ما كان نافعا في وقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spreading mercy means distributing blessings through the growth of plants and production of fruit caused by rain.
rows.anchor: ونشر الرحمة تفريق النعمة بين الناس بإنبات النبات وإخراج الثمار التي يكون سببها المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion shifts from provision to signs of divine unity connected with provision, and further signs follow.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية انتقال من حديث الرزق إلى آيات التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing names al-Walī and al-Ḥamīd praise God for His beautiful action.
rows.anchor: وتذييل الآية بالاسمين الولي الحميد وهما من أسمائه تعالى الحسنى للثناء عليه في فعله الجميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: B-th-th means scattering or dispersing; dābba covers all creatures that move over the earth, hence animals generally.
rows.anchor: والدابة كل ما يدب على الأرض فيعم الحيوانات جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s apparent meaning is that creatures exist in the heavens as on Earth; he rejects the view that these are angels because dābba is not customarily used for angels.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية أن في السماوات خلقا من الدواب كالأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh made his people’s minds and judgment foolish, and so they obeyed him.
rows.anchor: استخف عقول قومه وأحلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are described as transgressors and sinners.
rows.anchor: إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āsafūnā means they angered or displeased God; divine anger means the will to punish.
rows.anchor: والغضب منه تعالى إرادة العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salaf means those who came before; Pharaoh’s people preceded later peoples in entering the Fire.
rows.anchor: السلف المتقدم والظاهر أن المراد بكونهم سلفا للآخرين تقدمهم عليهم في دخول النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathal is an oft-repeated example; their becoming an example means later people could learn from them if they reflected and took warning.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن كونهم مثلا لهم كونهم مما يعتبر به الآخرون

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: Tafsīr al-Qummī explains the phrase about Moses as meaning that he did not make his speech clear.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { ولا يكاد يبين } قال لم يبين الكلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says God does not become angry as humans do; He made chosen guides whose pleasure and displeasure count as His because they call people to Him, without creaturely emotions reaching God.
rows.anchor: إلى أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل { فلما آسفونا انتقمنا منهم }

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The report argues that if grief or irritation affected God, change and possible extinction would follow, erasing the distinction between Creator and created; it cites obedience to the Messenger and allegiance to him as allegiance to God.
rows.anchor: ولو كان يصل إلى المكون الأسف والضجر وهو الذي أحدثهما وأنشأهما لجاز لقائل أن يقول إن المكون يبيد يوما

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The author notes a similar report in al-Kāfī through Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Bazīʿ, his uncle Ḥamza b. Bazīʿ, and al-Ṣādiq.
rows.anchor: وروى مثله في الكافي بإسناده عن محمد بن إسماعيل بن بزيع عن عمه حمزة بن بزيع عنه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtilā means forcibly shaking, pushing, or driving someone.
rows.anchor: الاعتلاء الزعزعة والدفع بعنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ al-jaḥīm means the middle of Hell.
rows.anchor: وسواء الجحيم وسطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is addressed to the angels assigned to Hell: seize the sinner and drive him violently to its center so it envelops him.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للملائكة الموكلين على النار أي نقول للملائكة خذوا الأثيم وادفعوه بعنف إلى وسط النار لتحيط به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links Hell’s enveloping the sinner to the statement that Hell surrounds the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added phrase “of the torment of boiling water” is explanatory: pour over his head the boiling water with which he is punished.
rows.anchor: وإضافته إلى الحميم بيانية والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinner is addressed while enduring successive punishments.
rows.anchor: خطاب يخاطب به الأثيم وهو يقاسي العذاب بعد العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the sinner mighty and noble while he is abject and vile is mockery that intensifies his punishment.
rows.anchor: وتوصيفه بالعزة والكرامة على ما هو عليه من الذلة واللأمة استهزاء به تشديدا لعذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The irony recalls his worldly belief that he had honor and a good outcome with God.
rows.anchor: وقد كان يرى في الدنيا لنفسه عزة وكرامة لا تفارقانه كما يظهر مما حكى الله سبحانه من قوله

words: إِنَّ هَذَا مَا كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَمْتَرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imtirāʾ means doubt and uncertainty.
rows.anchor: الامتراء الشك والارتياب

words: إِنَّ هَذَا مَا كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَمْتَرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement may continue the tormentors’ address, underscoring the disbelievers’ error in doubting the punishment they now see directly.
rows.anchor: وفيها تأكيد وإعلام لهم بخطئهم وزلتهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is described as tasting because taste expresses full perception of pains and pleasures.
rows.anchor: ولذا عبر عن تحمل العذاب بالذوق لما أنه يعبر عن إدراك ألم المولمات ولذة الملذات إدراكا تاما بالذوق

words: إِنَّ هَذَا مَا كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَمْتَرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God may begin a new address to the unbelievers; the plural “you doubted” may support this because the preceding address is singular.
rows.anchor: استئنافا من كلام الله سبحانه يخاطب به الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqām is a place of standing, stability, or residence; amīn means secure from harm, so the righteous are established in a place wholly safe at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: المقام محل القيام بمعنى الثبوت والركوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the place itself secure is a figure of speech that attributes the quality of safety to the location.
rows.anchor: وبذلك يظهر أن نسبة الأمن إلى المقام بتوصيف المقام بالأمين من المجاز في النسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens and springs explain the secure station; springs are a setting by adjacency because they lie within the gardens.
rows.anchor: وجعل العيون ظرفا لهم باعتبار المجاورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural gardens may reflect different kinds of gardens or that each person has one or more gardens.
rows.anchor: وجمع الجنات باعتبار اختلاف أنواعها أو باعتبار أن لكل منهم وحدة جنة أو أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus is fine silk and istabraq is thick silk; both words are Arabicized from Persian.
rows.anchor: السندس الرقيق من الحرير والإستبرق الغليظ منه وهما معربان من الفارسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They sit facing one another for companionship, since no evil or harm exists in their secure abode.
rows.anchor: أي يقابل بعضهم بعضا للاستيناس إذ لا شر ولا مكروه عندهم لكونهم في مقام أمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika means that their state is as described.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر كذلك أي كما وصفناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairing them with houris means making them companions; zawj’s basic linguistic sense is companion.
rows.anchor: والمراد بتزويجهم بالحور جعلهم قرناء لهن من الزوج بمعنى القرين وهو أصل التزويج في اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥūrāʾ describes intense whiteness and blackness of the eye, or a dark pupil like a gazelle; ʿaynāʾ means large-eyed.
rows.anchor: والحور جمع حوراء بمعنى شديدة سواد العين وبياضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that the houris are distinct from earthly women who enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: وظاهر كلامه تعالى أن الحور العين غير نساء الدنيا الداخلة في الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Zayd al-Shaḥḥām reports al-Ṣādiq saying that the People of the Household are the exception God made, and that they can benefit others through intercession.
rows.anchor: عن زيد الشحام قال قال لي أبو عبد الله عليه السلام ونحن في الطريق في ليلة الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the report as a reference to intercession and takes the exception from the first occurrence of mawlā in the verse.
rows.anchor: إلى الشفاعة وقد أخذ الاستثناء

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: Tafsīr al-Qummī says the verse about the zaqqūm tree as food for the sinner was revealed concerning Abū Jahl b. Hishām.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: Tafsīr al-Qummī glosses muhl as molten yellow copper and ḥamīm as water heated to its utmost.
rows.anchor: قال المهل الصفر المذاب { يغلي في البطون كغلي الحميم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes that reports in Sunni sources also support the verse’s revelation concerning Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: ومن طرق أهل السنة أيضا روايات تؤيد نزول الآية في أبي جهل
